Greece Cruise Packages & Greek Island Cruises 2026–2027

blocks.text: A Greek island cruise lets you wake up somewhere new without packing your suitcase every morning. One day may begin in Mykonos, another in Santorini or Rhodes, while your cabin stays with you throughout the sailing.

Our Greece cruise packages follow several routes through the Aegean. Some concentrate on the Cyclades, others travel farther toward Rhodes or the Turkish coast, and selected itineraries combine the cruise with hotel nights and sightseeing in Athens or elsewhere in Greece.

What is included depends on the sailing. Cruise accommodation and selected meals are generally part of the cruise section, while some packages also include hotels, airport or port transfers, guided sightseeing, or shore excursions. Check the individual itinerary for the exact route and inclusions.

sections.heading: What Kind of Cruise Are You Looking For?

blocks.text: Start with how you want to spend your time, not simply how many islands appear on the route.
A Cyclades cruise keeps the focus on islands such as Mykonos, Naxos, Paros, and Santorini. It works well when the Aegean islands themselves are the main reason for the trip.
Other sailings continue farther south toward Rhodes or include additional Aegean ports, giving you a wider geographical route.

There are also cruises that cross between Greece and Turkey, with selected sailings calling at ports on the Turkish Aegean coast. Kusadasi, for example, provides access to Ephesus and creates a very different port day from those spent on the Greek islands.
Then there are cruise-and-land journeys, where the ship is only one part of the vacation.
These can be a good choice if you want to see several islands from the water but still spend proper time in Athens or another destination before or after sailing.

sections.heading: How Much Time Do You Actually Get Ashore?

blocks.text: This is one of the most useful things to check before choosing a cruise.
Two itineraries can visit the same island but give you very different days there. One ship may stay in port through the evening; another may leave after only a few hours.
Look at the scheduled arrival and departure times, not only the list of ports.
This matters particularly in places such as Santorini and Mykonos, where a short daytime call feels quite different from having enough time to stay into the evening.
A longer list of islands is not necessarily a better cruise if most of those visits are brief.

sections.heading: What Is Life Like Between the Islands?

blocks.text: The ship is part of the holiday, not simply transportation.
Instead of checking out of one hotel, travelling to a ferry port, moving your luggage, and checking into another hotel, you return to the same cabin after each port visit.
Meals and onboard facilities depend on the vessel and package. Some cruises place more emphasis on the ship itself, while others are primarily about reaching a new port each day.
Before booking, check the ship, cabin category, meal arrangements, and time spent sailing alongside the destination list.
Those details can have as much impact on the trip as the route.
If Athens is important to you, do not assume that seeing it briefly before embarkation is enough.

A cruise-and-land package can add hotel nights before or after sailing, giving you time for the Acropolis, historic Athens, or other parts of mainland Greece without trying to fit them around embarkation times.
The same principle applies to island extensions. Spending several nights on an island after the cruise gives you a very different experience from visiting it for a few hours as a port of call.
Cruising gives you variety. Staying on land gives you time.
Combining the two can give you both.

sections.heading: When to Take a Greek Island Cruise

blocks.text: The main Aegean cruise season runs through the warmer months, with a wider range of departures during late spring, summer, and early autumn.

May, June, September, and early October are attractive for travelers who want warm conditions without the busiest part of midsummer. July and August bring strong demand and a lively atmosphere at popular island ports.
Schedules are seasonal, however, and not every route operates throughout the entire period. Always compare the actual departure dates for the cruise you are considering.

sections.heading: Is a Cruise the Right Way to See Greece?

blocks.text: Choose a cruise if you like the idea of seeing several islands while unpacking only once.

If you would rather spend two or three nights on each island, choose your own restaurants in the evening, and have unscheduled days ashore, a hotel-based itinerary may suit you better. Our Greece Travel Packages use hotels with ferry or flight connections instead.
For travelers who prefer a structured journey primarily on land, see our Greece Escorted Tours.
You can also browse our main Greece Tours collection to compare the different ways of travelling through Greece.

faqs.q: What is included in Greece cruise packages?
faqs.a: Greece cruise packages include: a licensed guide for all shore excursions at archaeological sites, cabin accommodation on the cruise vessel with full board (three meals daily), Athens hotel with daily breakfast, private transfers between Athens hotel and Piraeus port, and all port taxes. International flights from your home country are not included. Some packages include domestic flights within Greece if the cruise departs from a port other than Piraeus.

faqs.q: Which Greek islands are usually visited on a cruise?
faqs.a: Standard 7-night cruises from Piraeus typically cover Mykonos, Patmos, Rhodes, Heraklion (Crete), and Santorini. Alternative routes add Kusadasi (for Ephesus, Turkey), Corfu, Kefalonia, or Zakynthos. Small-vessel cruises can be customised to include Amorgos, Symi, Kastellorizo, Hydra, or Spetses.

faqs.q: Are Greece cruises suitable for first-time travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Greece cruise packages are one of the most accessible formats for first-time visitors to Greece. The cruise handles accommodation, transport between islands, and most meals in a single arrangement. Licensed guides for shore excursions are included at all archaeological sites. The Athens portion before or after the cruise provides the mainland context.

faqs.q: Can I customise my Greece cruise package?
faqs.a: Yes, on small-vessel cruises of up to 50 passengers. Route, cabin category, departure date, and shore excursion selection can all be customised on private charters or semi-private small-vessel bookings. Large cruise ship itineraries follow fixed routes. Contact us with your preferred islands and dates to build a custom cruise program.

faqs.q: Do Greece cruise packages include guided shore tours?
faqs.a: Yes. A licensed English-speaking guide is included for shore excursions at all major archaeological sites: the Acropolis in Athens (required by Greek law), Knossos in Crete, the medieval Old City in Rhodes, and the Monastery of Saint John on Patmos. At non-archaeological ports (Mykonos, Santorini), a local guide is included for the first hour orientation; the remainder of the port time is at your discretion.

faqs.q: How much does a Greece cruise package cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Eight to ten day Greece cruise packages (2 nights Athens plus 7-night cruise) cost approximately 2,200 to 3,800 USD per person based on double occupancy in a standard cabin, depending on vessel category, season, and cabin type. Small-vessel private charters cost significantly more per person but allow full customisation. Contact us for a current quote for your preferred dates and vessel type.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a Greece cruise and island hopping by ferry?
faqs.a: A cruise provides accommodation on the vessel, meals included, and a guided escort throughout. Island hopping by ferry uses land-based hotel accommodation on each island and scheduled public or private ferry connections. Cruises are more convenient logistically and suit shorter trips. Ferry-based island hopping allows longer stays on each island and more flexibility in itinerary. Magnificent Travel offers both formats.

faqs.q: Can the Greece cruise be combined with Turkey?
faqs.a: Yes. Some cruise routes from Piraeus include a port call at Kusadasi in Turkey, from which Ephesus is a 30-minute drive. For a fuller Turkey program alongside Greece, Turkey and Greece tours run 10 to 14 days and include Istanbul, Cappadocia, Athens, and Santorini connected by flights.
